analysis.evidence: Enoch is the subject, and אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים means “with God.” The duration שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה (“three hundred years”) presents this walking as Enoch’s habitual way of life.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ־ marks the narrative sequence. The verb is Hithpael wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with חֲנוֹךְ.
analysis.sense: conduct one’s life in fellowship with God

analysis.evidence: חֲנוֹךְ is the subject of וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ, “he walked.” The phrase אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “after he fathered Methuselah,” identifies him as the Enoch in Jared’s line.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ חֲנוֹךְ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים, Enoch is the subject of וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ ‘walked’, and אֶת introduces הָאֱלֹהִים as the one with whom he walked.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition in the short form אֶת, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ חֲנוֹךְ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים, “Enoch walked with God,” אֶת means “with,” and הָאֱלֹהִים identifies God as the one with whom Enoch walked.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ prefixes a masculine plural absolute common noun. The noun refers here to God in the singular.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי introduces הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “he fathered Methuselah.” Enoch walked with God for three hundred years after that event.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the plural construct form אַחֲרֵי, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מְתוּשֶׁלַח means “after he fathered Methuselah.” The suffix refers to Enoch, and אֶת marks Methuselah as the direct object.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with the third-person masculine singular suffix ־וֹ marking the subject, Enoch.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “after he fathered Methuselah,” אֶת marks the proper name מְתוּשֶׁלַח as the direct object of הוֹלִידוֹ.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ אֶת מְתוּשֶׁלַח, “after he fathered Methuselah,” אֶת marks Methuselah as the direct object. Enoch is the father.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשׁ counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. Together with שָׁנָה ‘year’, the phrase gives the duration of Enoch’s walk with God after Methuselah’s birth as three hundred years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular cardinal numeral in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, שְׁלֹשׁ counts the hundreds and שָׁנָה supplies the unit, giving the duration of Enoch’s walk with God as three hundred years after he fathered Methuselah.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה means “three hundred years.” It measures the portion of Enoch’s life during which he walked with God after he fathered Methuselah.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Enoch is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and בָּנִים וּבָנוֹת (“sons and daughters”) are its direct objects.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix
